messages:
mira: heads-up — after the kernel-autotune merge i see p99 regressions for a subset of 8k-seq production workloads. batch_shape histogram is skewing to many small-batches with long seq_len. anyone seen similar?
raj: which commit? autotune v2 (kernel-cost-model) or the later tweak to launch-weighting?
lucas: the v2 merge + the tweak landed in prod yesterday (rollout 50%). i've got a quick flame/prof dump. paste:```
sampled_batches: {sizes: [1,2,3,1,1,2], seq_lens: [6400,6400,6400,8192,2048,6400]}
kernel_picks: [matmul_fused_v1, matmul_fused_v1, matmul_fused_v2, matmul_standard, matmul_fused_v1, matmul_fused_v2]
launch_ms: [0.36, 0.36, 0.48, 0.12, 0.36, 0.48]
steady_state_ms_per_token: [0.0009,0.0009,0.0007,0.0011,0.0009,0.0007]
```
lucas: note how for size==1, autotune sometimes picks v1 (higher steady token cost) because launch-weight calculus was off for very long seqs.
olga: hmm looks like kv-cache warmup + continuous batching producing lots of single-request batches for long seqs. kernel selector favors lower per-token cost but ignores the extra launch overhead at seq-length extremes.
raj: can we reproduce with the local simulator? i suspect the cost model is using mean batch_size not the tail.
perf-bot: nightly-regression: p99 latency +18% on job x86-prod-8k since 1978878000, test-suite "long-seq-contbatch" failed threshold. (regression id r-1978879999)
mira: plan proposal: augment cost model to include batch_shape-aware term: launch_cost * (1 - exp(-batch_size)) + steady_cost*tokens. quick pseudo:```
cost(kernel, batch) = launch_ms(kernel) * batch_weight(batch.size) + steady_ms_per_token(kernel) * total_tokens
where batch_weight(s) = 1 - exp(-s / 2.0)  # so singletons keep most launch penalty
```
raj: i like that. also we should add seq_len quantiles into the tuner input so it knows when long sequences dominate.
olga: also check KV-cache warmup heuristic — when cache miss ratio > 0.2 we should bias toward kernels with lower launch overhead until cache warms.
lucas: i'll run a small ablation on canary (flag: kernel_cost_shape_v1) and compare p50/p95/p99. will post numbers.
mira: for rollout: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with realtime perf alerts. add automatic rollback if p99 increases >10% for 10m.
raj: also add unit test that simulates continuous-batching churn: varying arrival rates + seqlen mix, assert selector picks kernel A for (size=1, seq>=6k).
perf-bot: test created: long-seq-contbatch-sim v1, assigned to lucas. run id t-1978880002.
mira: great. lucas, please include a tiny instrumentation change to log kernel_choice_reason (cost components) for 1% traffic so we can inspect.
lucas: will do. starting experiments now. :thumbsup:
raj: optional: we can try a micro-optimization to make launch_ms cheaper (kernel prewarm) but that's a backup if cost-model tweaks insufficient.
mira: thanks all — follow up in this thread with numbers. :eyes:
